meta.name: Silo Agent
meta.summary: A multi-user agent host: each Bot is a durable container with a desktop, driven by an agent loop in a Go control plane that talks to model providers, gates every tool call through rules and approvals, and filters what the Bot reads. Bots are reached from a React console, an iOS app, chat apps, a receive-only mailbox and tunnels; all their internet traffic leaves through a filtering egress gateway.

flows.name: Sign in
flows.summary: Password sign-in with throttling and an optional authenticator code; the session cookie is the only credential the console holds.

steps.detail: The sign-in page sends email + password, and the code only once the server asked for one.
Failures per account+address (5, then a doubling wait), per address and per account; the address is the peer unless it is a trusted proxy.
The hash is checked even when no user matched, so a miss takes as long as a hit.
The failure is counted against the limiter.
No pending state is kept: the client resends email + password + code.
A conditional update on the used time step, so a code cannot be replayed or raced.
With auth.host_cookie on, the cookie is __Host-silo_session and the plain name is never read.

flows.name: Send a chat message
flows.summary: One run per chat: stream model turns, run tools on the Bot's box.

steps.text: Own the Bot and chat; writable?
steps.detail: ownBot/ownChat scope to the signed-in user; automation and subagent logs are read-only.
The New chat page makes the row with this message; a refused send deletes it again.
One live run per conversation; a message during a run is injected into its inbox instead.
Always confirms the box with the engine even with a live worker session; creates it on the Bot's own egress network if gone.
History is rebuilt byte for byte from the log so the provider's prompt cache keeps hitting.
System prompt built once per run in cache tiers; thinking level fitted to the model.
A provider context-length error triggers one summary of the history and a retry of the turn.
Every tool goes through one engine: surface check, the rule (Allow/Auto/Ask/Deny), then the handler.
Queued on the worker's Commands stream; the run's first file-changing tool takes a Changes snapshot first.
Chunks stream to the thread live; done resolves the waiting call with masked output.
Output is filtered, masked and capped at 12000 bytes before the model or the log sees it.
The client replays persisted events and reconnects with after_event_id.

flows.name: Python calls a gated tool
flows.summary: Code in exec_python calls a connector through silo_runtime; the CP applies the same rule as a chat tool, may ask the owner, and filters what comes back.

steps.detail: silo_runtime.call posts connector, action, args and SILO_RUN_ID to the worker's socket.
The bot token is looked up by hash; the call belongs to a chat only while that run is live on this Bot.
A locked operator rule is a floor the owner can only tighten.
Policy + action + the human's latest message; anything unclear, an error or a 30 s timeout becomes Ask, never Allow.
Arguments are redacted; the Bot's status becomes needs_you.
always writes an Allow rule, except on an Auto rule's slip, where it counts as allow_once.
Connector headers and OAuth stay on the CP; a gone session is redialed once.
Connector results default to Check; the verdict frames, withholds or passes the result.
A script must not carry on as if it had the data; the warning rides on the cell's own result.
Prose is wrapped as {"result": text}; the thread shows a call / call_result row.

flows.name: Use a secret on the web
flows.summary: The box only ever holds a stand-in; the egress gateway swaps the real value in on the way to the secret's allowed hosts and blocks it anywhere else.

steps.detail: In surrogate mode, behind a filtering gateway, the box gets the stand-in; both values are masked from the log.
The box sits on its own --internal network whose only way out and DNS is the gateway.
Block lists, threat feeds, private addresses, then surrogate leaks; flags for exfil sinks and secret shapes.
Reported to the CP as an alert in the Audit tab.
Headers only, unless the owner allowed body swaps for that secret.

flows.name: Mail wakes a Bot
flows.summary: Each Bot has a receive-only address; a verified mail from a listed sender starts a run in a new chat.

steps.detail: Unknown recipients count toward a per-address probe limit (451 past it).
A store failure answers 451 so the sender retries.
DMARC's alignment test without the policy lookup; nothing is rejected over it.
Deduped by (bot_id, sha256); the newest 200 are kept.

flows.name: Open a private tunnel
flows.summary: A Bot's localhost service gets an address on the CP; private ones hand off the owner's Silo session without the session cookie ever leaving the CP origin.

steps.detail: A disabled owner's tunnels are 404 to everyone.
The grant lives only as long as the Silo session that made it, and only for the Bot's current owner.
Then a 30 s single-use ticket is redeemed at /.silo/auth; API calls get a plain 401.
A tunnel request never starts a box.
5900 (VNC) and 9222 (Chromium) are refused on both ends.
Both ends wrap the stream in a net.Conn, so keep-alive and upgrades need no special code.

flows.name: Automation fires
flows.summary: A scheduler tick fires due cron automations exactly once, each run starting from a fresh context in a hidden log chat.

steps.detail: Cron in the Bot's time zone; only the writer that moves next_run_at fires.
Never queued.
The log does not grow with each firing; state lives in files or memory.
Web search is Python-only: one gated call, a batch of up to 10 queries.
Each scraped site has a token bucket shared across Bots (1 request / 6 s); a stuck source is never waited on past 4 s.
web.search results are checked by the output filter by default.

flows.name: Telegram message in, reply out
flows.summary: A channel binds one Bot to one picked chat; inbound text starts or steers a run and only finished sections go back.

steps.detail: Private chats always get a reply.
Thinking and tool output stay in the log; presented files are attached as real bytes.

components.name: Control plane
components.role: Users, Bots, agent loop, tool engine, rules and approvals, output filter, connectors, channels, mail, tunnels; serves the console and every sidecar link.

components.name: Worker
components.role: Dials the CP, runs commands (Python kernels, terminal, files, desktop), serves silo_runtime over a unix socket, tunnels VNC/console/ports.

components.name: Bot box
components.role: The Bot's durable machine with a desktop; /workspace is bound from data/.

components.name: Egress gateway
components.role: The only way out for boxes and STDIO sidecars: blocks, flags, swaps surrogate secrets, reports traffic.

components.name: Drive sidecar
components.role: Mounts cloud drives into /workspace/drives and journals changes; holds every drive credential.

components.name: STDIO MCP sidecar
components.role: Runs a STDIO MCP server and pumps JSON-RPC to the CP over MCPHost.Tunnel.

components.name: Web console
components.role: Chats, panes (Files, Desktop, Console, Changes, Mail), Customize, Settings, Admin.

components.name: iOS app
components.role: Native client of the same UI service.

data.name: users / sessions / invites
data.holds: Accounts, hashed sessions, invite and reset links, TOTP state

data.name: bots / secrets / rules / operator_rules
data.holds: Bots with SOUL and CORE MEMORY, secrets with surrogates, call and output rules in two layers

data.name: chats / runs / run_events
data.holds: Conversations and the append-only event log replayed as model history

data.name: approvals / audit_events / llm_logs
data.holds: Approval slips, every gate/filter/network decision, raw model traffic

data.name: memories / memory_digests
data.holds: Long-term memories as vector(1536) and their digest

data.name: knowledge_folders / sources / chunks
data.holds: RAG index of workspace folders (vector + tsv)

data.name: connectors / bot_connectors / drives
data.holds: Library presets, per-Bot copies with OAuth, drive specs and tokens

data.name: automations / subagents / task_items / feed_posts
data.holds: Schedules, background agents, taskboards and the owner's feed

data.name: tunnels / tunnel_grants / mailboxes / mail_*
data.holds: Tunnel addresses and session-bound grants, mailboxes and received mail

data.name: egress_*
data.holds: Gateway hosts, client networks, patterns, CA, per-minute traffic

data.name: data/bots/<id>
data.holds: Workspace, Chrome profile, shadow git history, npm cache (files, not Postgres)

guards.checks: Session cookie (hashed lookup); only SignIn, AuthOptions, GetInvite, AcceptInvite are public

guards.limit: 5 per account+address, then doubling 30 s → 15 min
guards.checks: Constant-time miss, TOTP step stored, recovery codes crossed off
Per-Bot bearer token looked up by hash
Rule Allow / Auto / Ask / Deny, operator floor, approval slip
Output rule Pass / Flag / Check / Withhold; filter voice defanged
No relay, no AUTH; DKIM/SPF verified flag; wake ≤ 10/h
Grant bound to a live session and the current owner
Internal network; gateway blocks threats, private addresses and surrogate leaks
Conditional claim; skip if previous run live

unknowns: Production deployment (host, TLS termination, region) is not in the repository; only docker-compose.dev.yml for Postgres, Lightpanda, smtp4dev, Radicale and Dex.
There is no general per-user rate limit on UI RPCs such as Send; throttling exists only for sign-in, codes and invite tokens.
The WhatsApp and Discord adapters follow the same DeliverInbound path as Telegram but were not traced line by line here.
Drive sidecar internals (rclone supervision, journal) and the STDIO bridge were not traced as flows.
tmp/ddgs (a FastAPI search service) is in the tree but nothing in the Go code calls it.
